newsitem.title: UK: East Midland closes up on bid hopes.
newsitem.headline: East Midland closes up on bid hopes.

text.p: Shares in East Midlands Electricity rose in late trade on Tuesday after a source close to the UK electricity company said it would meet its potential bidder, Dominion Resources of the U.S., at 1700 GMT.
But traders and analysts said the market remained unconvinced that the American utility would launch a bid, and the stock closed up 7.5p at 611p, down from an earlier high of 620p.
Nigel Hawkins, utilities analyst at Yamaichi, said Dominion would need to start bid talks at 650p per share to have a realistic chance of winning a recommendation from East Midlands.
But he added that East Midlands was unlikely to recommend a bid below 700p per share.
"I do not believe East Midlands would recommend a bid siginficantly below 700p per share. I am not saying they would refuse it at the 690p level," said Hawkins.

Dominion said last week that it was interested in bidding for East Midlands, but added it would not offer much more than 608p per share. East Midland said it would advise shareholders to reject any bid at that level.
But traders emphasised that Dominion could still walk away from the bid talks amid regulatory and political uncertainties.
Some said they believed it unlikely that Dominion would offer much more than 608 pence, which would value East Midlands at about 1.2 billion stg.
